subject: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist - FinTechCo
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks for the demo — perf targets and a couple clarifications

Marissa / Aditya,

Thanks for the demo today — that was really helpful. As we talked about on the call, the key performance requirements for our payments fraud-check feature are:

- Peak sustained throughput: ~25 requests/sec (each request is a short prompt, ~50-150 tokens)
- Concurrency target: support 40 concurrent outstanding requests during business spikes
- Latency SLO (end-to-end, 95th percentile): <= 300 ms for single-turn generation (non-streaming)
- Streaming behavior: first-byte/first-token latency <= 400 ms; steady-state per-token latency ideally <= 60 ms for streaming responses when returning longer explanations (up to 512 tokens)
- Availability: want guidance on how Redwood handles graceful degradation and fallback models if the preferred variant is unavailable

Can you confirm whether the model and config we saw on the demo can meet these targets in production? Also attaching our sample prompt set and the CSV you asked for (preliminary traffic shape).

Appreciate a concise checklist of the items you need from us to run a performance canary and any obvious blockers.

Best,
Alex
Lead PM, Fraud Detection
FinTechCo

Attachments: sample_prompts.txt, traffic_profile.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — perf targets and a couple clarifications

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the prompt set. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps:

Recap (high level):
- Model variant from demo (r-infer-medium-q4) is the recommended starting point for your latency/throughput mix.
- We believe the requirements you listed are achievable with: dedicated instance pool + intelligent batching and KV caching for repeated prefixes.

Immediate next steps (MAP):
1) Redwood to run a targeted performance canary using your sample prompts (we'll ab test two configs: quantized r-infer-medium-q4 and r-infer-medium-q8 with slightly different batching windows).
2) Aditya to provide a canary config (sched, concurrency limits, batch windows) and a rough cost estimate for the tested configs.
3) FinTechCo to confirm a 2-hour slot for canary traffic and supply synthetic traffic replay or a small inbound test token stream.
4) Redwood to deliver a perf report with 50/95/99 latency percentiles, CPU/GPU utilization, and failure modes, plus a recommendation for production rollout.

Questions for you:
- Do you want canary traffic to mimic peak-day patterns (spiky) or a steady-state sample? Our default is to start with a 30-min steady ramp, then 1-hour spiky run.
- Any regulatory constraints for storing prompt/response logs (for debugging canary runs)?

We'll also attach the demo recording and an initial SLO checklist. Proposed date for results: Monday, 23 Mar 2026. Does that work?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Schedule link: https://cal.redwood.com/marissa/30

Attachments referenced: demo-recording.mp4, slo-checklist.xlsx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — perf targets and a couple clarifications

Alex — quick technical notes / what we'll measure in the canary:

1) Latency expectations by prompt size (rough, depends on model selection & hardware):
   - Short prompts (<= 128 tokens): median ~40-70 ms per token, 95th ~150-250 ms end-to-end on a GPU-backed dedicated pool with small batching windows.
   - Medium prompts (~256 tokens): per-token steady state similar; first-byte may add 150-300 ms depending on KV warmup.

2) Streaming: we will instrument first-byte and per-token latencies. To meet your 400 ms first-byte target we recommend:
   - Keep initial decoding on a model variant that favors lower startup time (q4 tuned).
   - Use a smaller batching window for streaming requests to avoid batching-induced latency spikes.

3) Throughput & concurrency: your 25 req/s target with 40 concurrent is feasible with a small dedicated pool (2-4 GPUs) depending on model choice and request length. We'll dimension in the canary and provide sizing.

4) Graceful degradation: we'll demonstrate automatic fallback to a slightly smaller model variant and region failover in the canary to validate behavior. We can also show token-level cost tradeoffs.

I'll attach the initial benchmark script and the two canary configs. For the run, we need:
- Synthetic traffic file or permission to replay the attached traffic_profile.csv
- Expected percent of streaming vs non-streaming requests (rough split)
- Any IP whitelisting for the test harness

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: perf_canary_config_q4.yaml, perf_canary_config_q8.yaml, benchmark_runner.sh

From: Priya Menon <priya.m@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — perf targets and a couple clarifications

Thanks — couple quick clarifications from our infra team:

- For the canary we will replay traffic_profile.csv (attached earlier). That file includes both streaming and non-streaming samples. Streaming is ~30% of requests.
- We can provide a 2-hour window next Wednesday (25 Mar) 10:00-12:00 PST for the canary. Does Redwood prefer Monday as proposed or the Wed slot?
- On logs: we cannot share PII, but we can provide de-identified payloads for the run and accept temporary access to redwood's debug logs under an NDA.

If you can confirm the canary config and the exact inputs you need from us, we'll get the infra ticket raised.

Best,
Priya Menon
Staff Engineer, Platform
FinTechCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Priya Menon <priya.m@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — perf targets and a couple clarifications

Perfect, Priya — thanks for the timing and the details. Quick confirmations and decision criteria so everyone is aligned:

Confirmed canary scope:
- Date/time: Wed, 25 Mar 2026, 10:00-12:00 PST (FinTechCo confirmed).
- Traffic: replay of traffic_profile.csv (FinTechCo) with streaming ~30%, as stated.
- Configs: Redwood will run two configs (q4 & q8 variants) and provide 50/95/99 latencies, throughput, GPU utilization, error rates, and a suggested production sizing.

Decision criteria for production rollout (please confirm if this aligns with your internal bar):
- 95th percentile end-to-end latency <= 300 ms for short prompts and <= 500 ms for longer streaming sessions OR acceptable trading of cost vs latency documented.
- Throughput sustained at 25 req/s during spiky window without error-rate increase > 1%.
- Clear fallback demonstrated with <2x latency increase and acceptable output quality during simulated capacity loss.

Next steps / action owners:
- FinTechCo (Priya): raise infra ticket + provide de-identified payloads and IP allowlist (by Mon 23 Mar).
- Redwood (Aditya): deliver canary configs & runbook (today EOD).
- Redwood (Marissa): schedule results review for Thu 26 Mar or Fri 27 Mar (I'll send a poll).

I'll attach the SLO checklist and the recording again for reference. Looking forward to the run — we'll keep this lightweight and focused on the decision criteria above.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
